items.title: PMDC instructs medical, dental colleges not to admit Afghan students for 'current academic session'
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) has barred medical and dental colleges from granting admission or placement to Afghan students for the current academic session, and students previously enrolled in such programmes are “required to return to Afghanistan”, Dawn has learnt. The policy decision was conveyed by the council to public and private medical institutions across the country earlier this month. The PMDC communique, seen by Dawn , dated Sept 1, 2026, calls on all institutions to ensure the completion of administrative formalities to facilitate the departure of Afghan students. “It is further reiterated that Afghan nationals previously enrolled in medical or dental programs in Pakistan are required to return to Afghanistan, in accordance with the prevailing policy directions,” said the PMDC communique. “The concerned institutions shall ensure that all necessary administrative formalities, including issuance of requisite NOCs and facilitation of their departure are completed, accordingly,” added the council. The development came amid reports, circulating on social media, about the alleged expulsion of Afghan nationals who were studying at public sector medical colleges in Lahore. According to a health ministry official, an “in principle” decision had been made to send Afghan students enrolled in Pakistani medical universities back to their country, due to the ongoing tensions between Islamabad and Kabul. “Letters have been written to all medical universities asking their constituent colleges about the number of Afghan nationals enrolled in medical and dental colleges. Universities have also been directed to provide details of how many students are studying in each year,” he explained. The official said the PMDC had details of most Afghan medical students; however, “there remained a possibility that some may have been missed or mistakenly identified as nationals of other countries or as locals”. “After getting the information, lists will be shared with the concerned quarters, and the rest will be decided by them,” he said. However, he also clarified that the decision did not apply to students of other nationalities, only Afghan students. When asked about the reported expulsion of Afghan students, Foreign Office (FO) spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan told Dawn : “As per the Illegal Foreigner Repatriation Plan (IFRP), stay of any foreign national without a valid visa and passport is illegal, and the concerned individual is liable to deportation.” Khan added that Pakistani authorities were continuing to process visa extension applications from Afghan students “in line with our existing policy, rules and regulations”. The vice chancellor of a medical university confirmed receipt of the PMDC instructions, saying that institutions had begun collecting Afghan students’ particulars in line with the council’s instructions. “There were a number of students enrolled in undergraduate and postgraduate programmes. Although we were directed to provide the data, we were not told why such action was being taken,” he said. Millions of Afghans have poured into Pakistan over the past several decades, fleeing successive wars, including hundreds of thousands who arrived after the Taliban returned to power in 2021. In June, the Ministry of Interior issued a directive to immediately arrest any Afghan national “found residing in Pakistan without a valid visa” from July 10. A deportation drive first launched in 2023 was renewed in April last year when the government rescinded hun­dreds of thousands of residence permits for Afghans, warning them of arrests if they did not leave. Last year alone, over a million Afghan nationals were deported by Pakistan, a Senate Standing Committee on Kashmir Affairs, Gilgit-Baltistan and States and Frontier Regions (SAFRON) was informed. Pakistan deported a total of 1,155,221 Afghan nationals in 2025, top officials of the Ministry of Interior and Chief Commissionerate for Afghan Refugees told the meeting. The repatriation push also comes as relations between Pakistan and Afghanistan have deteriorated. Pakistan has repeatedly urged the Afghan Taliban government to rein in terrorist hideouts in Afghanistan and prevent militant groups from carrying out attacks against Pakistan from Afghan soil. However, its appeals have gone unheeded.

items.title: The 24-hour economy and Ghana’s MSMEs: A strategic roadmap for inclusive industrial transformation
items.description: The passage of the 24-Hour Economy Authority Act, 2025, and the subsequent signing of the 24-Hour Economy Authority Bill into law in February 2026, represent a watershed moment in Ghana’s structural transformation agenda. Yet, as someone who has had the stint of working with many companies under the 1D1F when I was heading the Business Resource Centre – Ada and a practitioner who has studied the dynamics of enterprise development, I contend that the success of this policy will ultimately be determined not by the elegance of its legislative framework, but by the extent to which it empowers and integrates Ghana’s Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises, the sector that accounts for approximately 85% of manufacturing employment and 70% of GDP. President John Dramani Mahama has been explicit that the 24-hour economy is “not simply about asking people to work at night”. Rather, it represents a deliberate strategy to utilise idle productive capacity, strengthen existing but under-utilised capacity, and create a continuum of economic activity that spans all hours. This nuanced framing is critical: the policy encompasses businesses that operate during the day with enhanced support, frontier firms that run multiple shifts, and the modernisation of entire value chains, particularly in agriculture, agro-processing, manufacturing, logistics, and digital services. The Binding Constraints: Where Theory Meets Practice Any dispassionate analysis must acknowledge the structural impediments that have historically constrained MSME productivity. Four critical bottlenecks demand attention: First, the financing gap approaches 6% of GDP. When SMEs adopt shift operations, working-capital requirements expand by nearly 18% to cover inventories, energy bills, and night-shift payroll, yet median loan tenure sits below 24 months, and collateral biases remain deeply entrenched. The Presidential Advisor for the 24-Hour Economy, Goosie Tanoh, has candidly observed that traditional collateral requirements often demand physical assets that are “unsustainable and continue to stifle innovation and private sector growth”. Second, energy reliability remains the Achilles’ heel. Ghana’s System Average Interruption Duration Index still exceeds 540 minutes per year, imposing direct outage costs of almost GH¢380 million on light manufacturing alone. Ewool Emmanuel, CEO of ESERB, a VCTF-backed mattress manufacturer in Tema, captured this reality succinctly: “The only challenge we have is erratic electricity… diesel generation compresses margins at a stage when the business is still establishing its revenue base”. High energy costs, averaging US$0.13–0.17 per kilowatt-hour, have eroded Ghana’s competitiveness relative to neighbouring countries. Third, labour-market rigidities and transport bottlenecks deter shift adoption. Night-shift premiums of up to 20%, limited enforcement of occupational-safety rules, and inadequate public transport after sundown suppress female participation to below 19% of night-shift employment. Extending business hours also changes community rhythms, necessitating local government action on licensing, policing, and sanitation. Fourth, digital and logistics frictions persist. Fewer than 31% of SMEs accept electronic payments, and last-mile delivery costs absorb almost 18% of retail price after 20:00. As the Ghana Enterprises Agency (GEA) CEO, Margaret Ansei, has emphasised, “President Mahama’s 24-hour economy is not just about extending business hours but it’s about reimagining productivity, creating jobs, and building businesses that run around the clock to do this, MSMEs need digital tools, infrastructure, and strategic partnerships”. Strategic Interventions: The Government’s Policy Toolkit My little research whilst at this article has shown the following interventions; namely, the government has responded with a comprehensive package of interventions that, if effectively implemented, could materially alter the feasibility calculus for MSMEs: Patient Capital: The Ghana Venture Capital Trust Fund (VCTF) has formalised a memorandum of understanding with the 24-Hour Economy Secretariat to establish a dedicated financing vehicle for SMEs intending to operate round the clock. This “patient capital” allows businesses time to stabilise and grow rather than focus on immediate returns. The VCTF has already catalysed more than GH¢2 billion in additional capital from private investors, with every cedi deployed mobilising GH¢5.58 from external sources. Portfolio companies have created over 28,000 jobs and remitted nearly GH¢47 million in taxes. Energy Cost Reduction: Plans are underway to reduce industrial electricity tariffs to between US$0.04 and US$0.07 per kilowatt-hour, more than halving energy costs for qualifying businesses. The Association of Ghana Industries (AGI) has specifically highlighted subsidised night-time electricity tariffs and fast-track import duty waivers for production equipment as essential tools for SME expansion. Modern Trading Infrastructure: The government has begun signing contracts for the construction of 24-Hour Economy Model Markets across all 261 districts. These modern, safe trading environments will incorporate solar lighting, cold storage, digital payment infrastructure, and enhanced security to support continuous commercial activity. Investment Readiness: The VCTF collaboration extends beyond funding to strengthening governance structures, ensuring regulatory compliance, and positioning SMEs to attract sustainable capital injections. The GEA is simultaneously rolling out programmes including the SME Innovation and Inclusion Programme, Digitalize for Jobs (D4J), and the U-Spark Project under the UNIDO KAIZEN Expansion Initiative. Incentive Framework: The 24-Hour Economy Authority Act integrates tax rebates for multi-shift operations and fast-track import duty waivers for production equipment. As the AGI has argued, while these measures may lead to a short-term dip in government revenue, the structural transformation they create will drive superior long-term fiscal stability. A Strategic Roadmap for MSMEs Drawing on international evidence and local realities, I propose the following strategic framework for MSMEs seeking to leverage the 24-hour economy: Embrace Sectoral Targeting. Productivity gains from extended hours are not automatic; they require demand at those hours, managerial capacity for multiple shifts, and cost structures that make night work profitable. MSMEs should focus on sectors where night activity already makes economic sense: food processing with perishable inputs, logistics and warehousing, selected manufacturing lines that can be scheduled in shifts, and digital services that can serve global markets across time zones. Pursue Investment Readiness. To access the patient capital being channelled through the VCTF, MSMEs must strengthen governance, ensure regulatory compliance, and develop credible business plans. As Michael Abbey, CEO of the VCTF, has indicated, the fund is already thinking about expansion projects, and businesses that demonstrate readiness will be best positioned to tap into dedicated SME financing. Leverage Digital Transformation. The digital economy is the natural ally of the 24-hour economy. MSMEs should aggressively adopt electronic payments, e-invoicing, and digital marketing. International evidence from Latin America shows that accelerated adoption of e-receipting systems lifts SME sales by 8% within two years while narrowing the VAT compliance gap. The GEA’s Digitalize for Jobs programme, supported by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development, provides a platform for this transition. Explore Cooperative Models. For micro-enterprises and informal operators, cooperatives can provide structure, solidarity, and scalability. Night Economy Cooperatives by sector or locality could secure access to group microloans, bulk purchasing power, and public procurement contracts. International best practice suggests establishing designated night market zones with solar lighting, security, and trader registration using Ghana Card-linked Night Economy IDs. Invest in Value Chain Integration. The 24-hour economy strategy explicitly envisions frontier firms nurturing SMEs and sourcing materials from them for operations, promoting both backward and forward linkages. MSMEs should position themselves as reliable suppliers to larger manufacturers and processors, leveraging the extended operating hours to meet just-in-time production schedules. Adopt Risk-Mitigation Strategies. Given the persistent energy constraints, MSMEs should explore cross-portfolio collaborations for renewable energy solutions. The VCTF is already pursuing this approach, linking a solar installation company in its portfolio with manufacturing companies facing similar difficulties. Time-of-use pricing that rewards off-peak activity can further reduce energy costs. A Call to Collective Action The 24-hour economy is not a panacea, nor is it a programme that can be imposed from above. As the AGI has rightly noted, the long-term sustainability of Ghana’s economic recovery depends heavily on diversifying the export base. The 24-hour economy provides the strategic framework; MSMEs must provide the entrepreneurial energy. The Ghana National Chamber of Commerce and Industry (GNCCI) has already mobilised to support this initiative, aiming to help over 2,000 SMEs scale their operations. The GNCCI President, Clement Osei-Amoako, has captured the essential truth: “The 24-hour economy will only succeed if manufacturers expand production, consumers drive demand, and financiers provide competitive lending rates. That is how we can turn policy into tangible growth”. Modelling suggests that if 20% of formal SMEs adopt dual-shift operations, national capacity utilisation could rise from 54% to 68%, lifting SME value added to 47% of GDP, generating 1.6 million additional jobs, and raising aggregate labour productivity by 15%. These figures are not predictions they are possibilities. Their realisation depends on the quality of implementation, the responsiveness of financial institutions, and the willingness of MSMEs to embrace innovation and restructuring. The policy tools are being assembled. The institutional framework is being established. The question that now confronts Ghana’s MSMEs is not whether the 24-hour economy will benefit them it is whether they will be strategic enough to benefit from.

items.title: HRW cautions against normalising ties with Taliban amid rights concerns
items.description: WASHINGTON: Human Rights Watch (HRW) has warned countries against normalising engagement with the Taliban without clear and measurable human rights benchmarks, as a UN expert highlighted the devastating consequences of five years of Taliban rule for Afghan children and young people. “Countries should not normalise engagement with the Taliban without clear and measurable human rights benchmarks,” HRW said in a statement to the UN Human Rights Council on Monday. It urged states to recognise gender apartheid as a crime against humanity and support International Criminal Court (ICC) efforts to prosecute those responsible for gender persecution and other grave international crimes in Afghanistan. The warning came as Richard Bennett, the UN special rapporteur on the human rights situation in Afghanistan, issued a new report on the impact of Taliban policies on children. Bennett said the Taliban’s institutionalised system of discrimination, repression and ideological control was depriving children of their rights to inclusive and quality education, freedom of expression and meaningful participation in social and public life. “Afghanistan’s children are growing up in an environment where discrimination, especially against girls and women, is being normalised; they are denied the right to learn and their opportunities for the future are dramatically shrinking,” Bennett said. He expressed particular concern over the continued denial of education beyond the sixth grade to girls and the growing exposure of children and young people to gender-based violence, forced and child marriage, child labour and ideological indoctrination. “These policies are not only violating children’s rights today — they are undermining their ability to determine their own futures,” Bennett said. “For girls in particular, the systematic denial of education is closing doors that may never reopen, with serious consequences for their mental health and the country’s development as a whole.” The report said these abuses were taking place against a backdrop of decades of conflict, poverty and unmet humanitarian needs. By dismantling or weakening institutions that previously protected children’s rights, the Taliban had exposed Afghan children to greater risks of violence, abuse and exploitation, Bennett said. Children living in poverty or remote areas, those with disabilities, members of marginalised religious and ethnic communities, and displaced children or those returning from abroad are among the most vulnerable, he said. Bennett also warned that restrictions on media, culture and freedom of expression were limiting the diversity of ideas and experiences available to Afghan children. “Children need space to learn, to think freely, to express themselves and imagine a different future,” he said. “Instead, many are growing up in fear, isolation and uncertainty.” The restrictions, combined with limited educational opportunities, were contributing to a growing sense of despair and could create future security concerns and a migration crisis, Bennett warned. He cautioned, however, against viewing Afghan children only as victims, noting their resilience and determination to support their families and communities and pursue alternative forms of learning. Bennett urged the Taliban to end discriminatory policies, restore comprehensive education for girls, strengthen child protection and justice systems, prevent child and forced marriage and child labour, prohibit corporal punishment, and restore inclusive healthcare and social protection for children with disabilities. He also called on other countries to fully fund humanitarian assistance, expand alternative education for girls and safe pathways for Afghans at risk, and support mine-action programmes, youth initiatives and international accountability efforts. “Five years of restrictive rule and socio-economic collapse have fundamentally altered the conditions in which Afghanistan’s children are growing up,” Bennett said. “The international community must act now to protect their rights and ensure that present and future generations are not deprived of the opportunity to shape Afghanistan’s future.” HRW, meanwhile, said gender persecution had become further entrenched over the past year, with the Taliban dismantling already limited legal protections for women and girls. “Since 2021, Taliban authorities have systematically deprived women and girls of their fundamental rights,” the organisation said. HRW cited a new criminal procedure code that recognises only “excessive” beating as domestic violence against women, potentially leaving survivors of other forms of abuse without effective avenues for justice. It also said a decree concerning judicial separation had eliminated minimum-age protections for girls’ marriage. Journalists, human rights defenders, peaceful protesters and former government employees continue to face arbitrary detention, enforced disappearance, torture and other serious abuses, HRW said. The organisation urged UN member states to renew Bennett’s mandate and provide his office with the resources needed to independently monitor and report on Afghanistan. It also called for the urgent operationalisation of the Human Rights Council’s new independent accountability mechanism for the country. HRW further urged governments not to forcibly return people to Afghanistan, where persecution remains systematic and well documented, and to support efforts by the International Criminal Court to prosecute those responsible for gender persecution and other grave international crimes. “Afghan victims, survivors and their families have waited far too long for truth, justice, and reparation,” HRW said. Separately, UN Secretary-General António Guterres renewed his call on the Taliban to lift restrictions preventing Afghan women working for the UN from entering its premises and carrying out their duties. The UN has said the restrictions hamper its ability to deliver assistance and services to the Afghan population, particularly women and girls. The warnings from Bennett, HRW and Guterres come as the Taliban regime approaches five years in power, with the UN expert warning that its policies are affecting not only the rights of Afghans today but the prospects of an entire generation of children.

items.title: Nigeria, Canada to set up joint team over visa delays
items.description: — To tackle irregular migration, removal of persons without legal status By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — The Federal Government and the Government of Canada have agreed to establish a joint technical working group to address persistent delays in the processing of Canadian visa applications by Nigerians and develop a framework for the removal of persons without legal status in Canada. Head, Press and Public Relations in the Ministry of Interior, Mary Ali, disclosed this in a statement issued yesterday in Abuja following a meeting between the Permanent Secretary in the ministry, Dr Magdalene Ajani, and the Chargé d’Affaires of the Canadian High Commission, David Sproule. According to the statement, both sides deliberated on delays in processing Canadian visa applications by Nigerian citizens, as well as opportunities under the expanding Nigeria-Canada Air Transport Agreement, ATA. Ajani, who represented the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, said prolonged visa processing times had affected Nigerians, including students. She said some Nigerian students had, on occasions, been unable to travel to Canada to commence their academic programmes because of delays in the issuance of study permits, even after their visa applications had been approved. Ajani stressed the need to address the concerns through sustained dialogue and stronger institutional cooperation between the two countries. The meeting also discussed the expansion of the Air Transport Agreement, which is expected to facilitate the introduction of direct flights between Nigeria and Canada, eliminating the need for passengers to connect through Europe or the United States. Both sides expressed optimism that the expanded agreement would boost commercial ties and improve convenience for travellers. On migration management, the meeting addressed the development of a Standard Operating Procedure, SOP, between Nigerian authorities and the Canada Border Services Agency, CBSA, for the removal of persons without legal status in Canada. Ajani assured the Canadian delegation that Nigeria would designate relevant officials to engage with their Canadian counterparts and facilitate the establishment of the joint working group. She reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation with Canada on immigration, travel facilitation and border management. Ajani also urged the Canadian authorities to give the concerns of Nigerian visa applicants due and expeditious consideration. Responding, Sproule acknowledged concerns over visa processing delays, describing the issue as an important pressure point in the bilateral relationship. He assured the Nigerian delegation that the concerns would be conveyed to the relevant Canadian immigration authorities, with a view to improving processing times and ensuring that Nigeria receives appropriate attention within the visa-processing system. Both sides agreed on the need to establish a small technical working group to drive the discussions and maintain regular engagement among relevant Nigerian and Canadian agencies. Sproule expressed appreciation for the openness of the Nigerian side and welcomed the ministry’s commitment to strengthening institutional cooperation between the two countries. The post Nigeria, Canada to set up joint team over visa delays appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Four years enough to transform Nigeria — Adebayo
items.description: — Says elites in Villa, govt houses are Nigeria’s problem — Challenges Tinubu to public debate By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party, SDP, Prince Adewole Adebayo, has said four years is enough for a determined government to transform Nigeria, urging voters to reject what he described as the country’s “politics of comedy and clowning.” Adebayo also identified what he described as the political elite occupying the Presidential Villa and state government houses as among the major problems confronting the country. He said bad leadership had been Nigeria’s primary problem since 1999, arguing that a change of government through the 2027 general election could significantly reduce insecurity. According to him, “It is the men in the Villa, government houses, that are the problem of Nigeria. We are promising that in four years we will defeat insecurity. When you use your vote in 2027 to change government, you have a chance of defeating 60 per cent of bandits.” Adebayo spoke yesterday in Abuja while unveiling the SDP’s 2027–2031 policy document, titled “Farewell to Poverty and Insecurity.” He described the document as the party’s blueprint for tackling Nigeria’s security, economic and infrastructure challenges. The SDP candidate also challenged President Bola Tinubu to a public debate ahead of the 2027 presidential election, while questioning the utilisation of funds associated with the removal of petrol subsidy. Adebayo accused the administration of failing to adequately account for funds he said were saved from subsidy removal and demanded explanations on spending on security, compressed natural gas, CNG, and electricity. He said, “The first challenge is thrown to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu: come out of hiding. Come and debate. “Anyone who wants to keep his job should be able to answer his bosses. Where have you been in the past four years? What have you been doing? Where is the money? “Where is the money you saved from subsidies that never existed? Where are the trillions for security? Where is the CNG? Where is the electricity?” Adebayo declared that “four years is enough for a determined leader to help his people,” insisting that an SDP administration would use its first term to fundamentally alter the country’s economic and security fortunes. He urged Nigerians to scrutinise the party’s manifesto and hold it accountable to the promises contained in the document. “We are trying to tell Nigerians that we are beyond sloganeering. We are saying to you: here is our farewell to poverty and insecurity. “We have submitted our thesis to Nigerians. Mark us. Evaluate us. Contradict us,” he said. On monetary policy, Adebayo criticised the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, alleging that it had failed to adequately protect the naira, promote productivity and create employment. “The Central Bank of Nigeria is not protecting our currency. It is not creating productivity and employment. It has become a warehouse for thieves. We must kick the thieves out of the team,” he alleged. He also alleged mismanagement of revenues from petroleum, solid minerals and taxation, describing public resources as being “stolen in broad daylight.” On insecurity, Adebayo said an SDP government would combine military action with political, economic and social interventions to address what he described as the root causes of crime and insurgency. He argued that government failure had contributed to insecurity and that changing the government through the ballot in 2027 would be a major step towards tackling banditry. He said, “Since the majority of insecurity is caused by government failure, when you use your vote in 2027 to change the government, you have already gone 60 per cent of the way towards chasing away the bandits.” On the economy, Adebayo pledged to promote national unity and tackle what he described as “internal colonialism,” which he said had encouraged ethnic, religious and regional divisions. He also promised to expand electricity generation to 75,000 megawatts using Nigeria’s available resources. Adebayo pledged to establish four functional public refineries and 36 modular refineries, while creating an enabling environment for private investors to establish additional refineries and export petroleum products. He also proposed a review of petrol pricing, arguing that Nigerians should not be subjected to international fuel prices when wages remained far below international standards. “That is why we calculated it and concluded that ₦200, at the current rate, is the price at which petrol can be sold without pushing the people further into poverty,” he said. Adebayo said the SDP manifesto would focus on human development, dignity of citizenship and affordable infrastructure financed from Nigeria’s resources. He lamented the decline in workers’ purchasing power, noting that previous generations were able to build houses and educate their children on incomes considerably lower than what many Nigerians require to survive today. “We are 26 years late. We need to be in government now,” he said. Earlier, SDP National Chairman, Prof. Sadiq Umar Gombe, said the manifesto was built around three interconnected pillars: security, productivity and prosperity. Gombe said the party would secure lives and property while addressing the economic and social conditions that fuel crime, extremism and instability. He said the SDP would strengthen the armed forces, police, intelligence agencies, border control and justice system, while deploying both kinetic and non-kinetic strategies against insecurity. According to him, the party’s economic programme would promote self-reliance, productive employment, poverty reduction, balanced regional development and social inclusion. “We do not believe that poverty should be managed in Nigeria. We believe poverty must be eliminated through production, employment, opportunity and responsible social protection,” Gombe said. He also stressed the need for accountability in public office, saying citizens must be able to demand answers from their leaders. “Accountability is not an inconvenience to governance. Accountability is governance itself,” he said. Gombe said the SDP wanted to build a Nigeria where farmers could cultivate their land without fear, traders could transport their goods safely, businesses could invest with confidence and citizens could live, work, worship and travel without fear. Also speaking, SDP vice-presidential candidate, Dr Usman Bugaje, said Nigeria’s fundamental problem was not a shortage of capable citizens but poor leadership. Bugaje pointed to the achievements of Nigerians in the diaspora as evidence that the country had the human resources required to build a prosperous nation. “If you look at Nigerians in the diaspora, they are doing very well. Go to any country and you will find Nigerian professionals performing at par with their counterparts. In many cases, they are excelling in their chosen fields. “That tells us something very important: the problem is not the Nigerian people. The problem is leadership,” he said. Bugaje described the manifesto as a commitment to Nigerians and a “living document” that would be refined through continued engagement with citizens. He identified low agricultural productivity and high energy costs as major constraints to national development, saying Nigeria could significantly improve food production by adopting proven agricultural methods and developing value chains. According to him, expensive energy affects virtually every sector, including transportation, agriculture and manufacturing. “We know precisely where the problems are, and I think we will, with the support of Nigeria, address them,” he said. Bugaje acknowledged that implementing the SDP agenda would face resistance from entrenched interests benefiting from the existing system. “They are going to fight. But we shall fight. And we shall win. And we shall deliver, God willing,” he said. The post Four years enough to transform Nigeria — Adebayo appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.description: Ouahigouya, 07 septembre 2026: une mission de visite de sites, de contrôle des travaux et de règlement de litiges a conduit le Directeur Général de la SONATUR dans la région du Yaadéga ce lundi 07 septembre. Accompagné de son staff technique et des responsables des entreprises en charge des travaux de viabilisation et d'assainissement, le camarade Directeur Général, Boureima OUATTARA, s'est rendu sur 3 sites de travaux dans la Commune de Ouahigouya. items.title: Malawi : un instituteur simule sa mort pour éviter de rembourser un prêt bancaire
items.description: Un instituteur originaire du district de Kasungu, au Malawi, a poussé l’audace à son paroxysme. C’est une histoire d’escroquerie aussi rocambolesque qu’improbable qui secoue actuellement la région de Kasungu. Pour échapper aux traites mensuelles et aux relances de son établissement bancaire, un enseignant du primaire a élaboré un stratagème radical : orchestrer sa propre mort administrative. Pris au piège par d’importantes dettes financières, l’homme a fabriqué de toutes pièces un dossier médical et un certificat de décès officiels. Ces documents falsifiés, une fois transmis à la banque, attestaient officiellement de son décès. Touchée par le prétendu drame qui frappait la famille de leur client, la direction de la banque a fait preuve de compassion en décidant d’effacer la totalité de la dette et d’annuler le contrat de prêt en cours. L’instituteur pensait alors avoir tiré un trait définitif sur ses soucis financiers. L’histoire aurait pu s’arrêter là, mais c’était sans compter sur l’amnésie ou la témérité de l’escroc. Quatre ans après avoir été déclaré mort par les services bancaires, l’instituteur, manquant de liquidités, a poussé la porte de la toute même agence bancaire. Présentant sa pièce d’identité en toute quiétude, il a formulé une nouvelle demande de prêt. C’est lors de la saisie de ses informations personnelles que le piège s’est refermé : le système informatique de l’établissement a immédiatement émis un alerte rouge, signalant que le demandeur était répertorié comme décédé depuis plusieurs années. Interpellés par cette anomalie et reconnaissant le visage du « défunt », les agents bancaires ont discrètement averti les forces de l’ordre. L’homme a été arrêté sur place par la police locale. Il est désormais poursuivi pour faux, usage de faux documents officiels et escroquerie à l’assurance/bancaire. items.title: Attack on Obi: Igbo Group demands apology from Governor Alia
items.description: — Condemns reported obstruction of NDC candidate’s visit By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki ABAKALIKI — The Igbo Renaissance Group has condemned the reported obstruction of the National Democratic Congress, NDC, presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi, from visiting communities affected by the recent killings in Benue State. The group also demanded a public apology from the Benue State Governor, Rev. Fr. Hyacinth Alia, to Obi over the reported incident. In a statement, the group’s chairman, Chief Emmanuel Igwe Chidi, called for an immediate investigation into the circumstances surrounding the alleged obstruction and the removal of any aide or official found responsible for ordering, organising or facilitating violence or obstruction. He also called on the Benue State Government to ensure that humanitarian assistance reached victims without political discrimination and renew its commitment to protecting the lives and dignity of residents regardless of political affiliation. Igwe urged Alia to ensure that political differences did not interfere with humanitarian efforts, stressing that public office should be used to promote service, compassion and reconciliation. He said the governor still had an opportunity to demonstrate the values of service and compassion associated with his previous clerical vocation. According to the group, Obi had alleged that his convoy was prevented from reaching communities affected by the Yelwata killings while attempting to express solidarity with victims and offer humanitarian assistance. The group said the allegation was disturbing, particularly at a time when affected families were mourning and communities were dealing with the aftermath of the attacks. It said: “Governor Hyacinth Alia must understand that the office of governor is greater than partisan politics. It is an office of service, compassion and responsibility. “If the reports concerning the obstruction of Mr Obi’s visit are correct, Governor Alia owes Nigerians, the victims of the Benue killings and, most importantly, Peter Obi a public explanation and apology. “We therefore call on Governor Alia to tender an unreserved public apology to Peter Obi within the next 24 hours and to immediately investigate the officials and aides allegedly involved in the incident. “Where any aide is found to have acted on the governor’s instructions or abused his office by mobilising people to obstruct a humanitarian visit, such an individual should be removed from office.” The group urged the governor to ensure that future humanitarian visits to affected communities were handled on the basis of security considerations rather than political affiliation. It also called on relevant security agencies to investigate the reported incident and establish the circumstances surrounding the obstruction. The post Attack on Obi: Igbo Group demands apology from Governor Alia appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Mahama raises concern over refereeing as Medeama, Nations FC receive support
items.description: President John Mahama has raised concerns about the standard of refereeing in Ghanaian football, warning that poor officiating is undermining confidence in the domestic league. According to the President, perceptions that some matches are decided before they are played are discouraging fans from attending games and, consequently, affecting clubs’ gate proceeds. “Unfortunately, refereeing is one of the things destroying our football,” President Mahama said. “Sometimes people believe the matches are decided before they are even played, and that makes the league less competitive.” President Mahama made the comments when Ghana Premier League champions Medeama Sporting Club, MTN FA Cup holders Nations FC and Ampem Darkoa Ladies paid a courtesy call on him ahead of their respective continental campaigns. He urged the Ghana Referees Association and the Ghana Football Association to work together to improve officiating standards and restore confidence in the league. “I want the Ghana Referees Association and the Football Association to work together to improve refereeing standards. Many spectators have stopped attending matches because they believe the outcomes are predetermined. That is reducing attendance and gate proceeds,” he said. President Mahama stressed the need for a competitive and credible domestic league, insisting that matches must be decided on merit. “It is in our interest to make the league competitive. Every match must be fairly officiated so that whoever wins does so on merit. That is the only way to restore confidence in our football,” he said. President Mahama also presented financial support to the three clubs as they prepare to represent Ghana in continental competitions. Medeama Sporting Club received GH¢342,000, equivalent to US$30,000. Nations Football Club received GH¢228,000, equivalent to US$20,000, while Ampem Darkoa Ladies Football Club received GH¢114,000, equivalent to US$10,000. The President also called for greater efforts to identify and nurture young talent, urging the Football Association to revive the Colts League, which he said had played an important role in developing young footballers. “We used to have a very good Colts League. I do not know what happened to it, so I want to ask the Football Association what has happened to the Colts League,” he said. “I hear it has been renamed grassroots football, but we all knew it as Colts. So, call it the Colts League, and let us all help to sponsor it.” He further criticised the early transfer of promising local players, arguing that the practice depletes the quality of the domestic league. “We must find a way to keep our talented players a little longer, give them opportunities in the national team, allow them to gain international experience, and then let them move abroad after they have matured,” he said. The President urged Medeama, Nations FC and Ampem Darkoa Ladies to perform strongly on the continent and help restore the glory days of Ghanaian football. “Go and recapture the glory days of Ghana football,” he said. “I want to travel abroad in the future, say I am from Ghana, and hear people proudly mention the names of our clubs once again.”

items.title: FNM : Mehdi Qotbi appelle à renforcer la formation des professionnels des musées au Maroc
items.description: Le président de la Fondation Nationale des Musées, Mehdi Qotbi, a appelé mardi à Rabat à investir davantage dans la formation des professionnels du secteur muséal, soulignant leur rôle essentiel dans la préservation de l’identité et du patrimoine marocains. La sauvegarde et la valorisation du patrimoine passent aussi par le renforcement des compétences de celles et ceux qui font vivre les musées. C’est le message porté mardi à Rabat par Mehdi Qotbi, président de la Fondation Nationale des Musées (FNM), à l’occasion d’une rencontre consacrée aux résultats d’une étude sur le développement d’une offre de formation spécialisée dans les métiers des musées et du patrimoine. « Accompagner le développement de nos musées, c’est aussi accompagner celles et ceux qui les dirigent, les animent, les préservent et les transmettent » , a souligné Mehdi Qotbi. Il a insisté sur la nécessité de renforcer les savoir-faire, de favoriser la circulation des connaissances et d’assurer une professionnalisation durable du secteur. Tenue au Musée Mohammed VI d’Art Moderne et Contemporain de Rabat, cette rencontre intervient dans le cadre d’un partenariat entre la FNM, l’Agence française de développement (AFD) et France Muséums, avec le soutien de l’ambassade de France au Maroc. Une formation adaptée aux besoins du secteur L’étude présentée lors de cette rencontre vise notamment à mieux cerner les évolutions du secteur muséal, à identifier les besoins actuels et futurs en matière de formation et à déterminer les compétences nécessaires au développement des institutions culturelles. Elle doit également contribuer à définir les futurs parcours de formation, les contenus pédagogiques, les publics ciblés ainsi que les modalités de gouvernance, les partenariats et le modèle économique nécessaires à la pérennisation d’un dispositif spécialisé. Pour Mehdi Qotbi, cette réflexion traduit une volonté de renforcer la coopération entre institutions et de mutualiser les expertises afin de préparer l’avenir des musées marocains. Un partenariat franco-marocain au service du patrimoine La directrice de l’AFD au Maroc, Catherine Bonnaud, a qualifié cette initiative de « projet emblématique » du partenariat franco-marocain. Elle a souligné l’importance de la formation des professionnels de la culture et des musées, au Maroc comme à l’échelle africaine. Selon elle, le soutien financier de l’AFD constitue un investissement dans le capital humain, la sauvegarde du patrimoine et le développement inclusif, avec l’ambition de contribuer au rayonnement culturel et artistique du Maroc et du continent africain. De son côté, Chloé Goupille, conseillère de coopération et d’action culturelle auprès de l’ambassade de France au Maroc et directrice générale de l’Institut français du Maroc, a présenté la formation des professionnels de la culture à l’échelle continentale comme une « priorité partagée » entre la France et le Maroc. Le Maroc ambitionne de renforcer son rôle en Afrique France Muséums considère également le projet comme une étape importante pour le développement du secteur. Son directeur général, Matthias Grolier, a estimé qu’une formation pérenne des professionnels pourrait contribuer à faire du Maroc un « interlocuteur muséal majeur sur la scène internationale ». L’étude estime par ailleurs que le Royaume dispose de plusieurs atouts pour devenir un acteur incontournable de la coopération muséale en Afrique, à condition de consolider les savoir-faire existants et de mettre en place une capacité de formation durable et adaptée aux réalités du secteur. À travers cette démarche, la Fondation Nationale des Musées entend ainsi structurer davantage l’écosystème muséal marocain, favoriser le partage des connaissances et renforcer les pratiques professionnelles, au service de la préservation et du rayonnement du patrimoine culturel national. The post FNM : Mehdi Qotbi appelle à renforcer la formation des professionnels des musées au Maroc appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Eguavoen appointed interim Super Falcons coach ahead of 2028 Olympic qualifiers
items.description: Former Super Eagles head coach Augustine “Cerezo” Eguavoen has been appointed to lead Nigeria’s Super Falcons on a temporary basis as the search for a permanent manager continues. His immediate assignment is navigating the 2028 Olympic Games second-round qualifying tie against Comoros this October. Eguavoen brings top-tier experience to the role, having previously guided the Super Eagles to a bronze medal at the 2006 Africa Cup of Nations in Egypt. Joining the interim technical crew is Nasarawa Amazons head coach Christopher Danjuma, who recently led the Falconets at the 2024 FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup. Former Super Falcons defender Ayisat Yusuf—who earned 68 caps and featured at the 2008 Beijing Olympics—also joins as an assistant coach, alongside veteran goalkeeper trainer Olatunji Baruwa. The 10-time African champions will kick off their campaign against Comoros, who advanced after a staggering 30-0 aggregate win over Sudan. Both legs of the fixture will take place at the Remo Stars Stadium in Ikenne-Remo on October 9 and 13, 2026. To secure one of Africa’s two spots at the Los Angeles 2028 Games, Nigeria must navigate four two-legged knockout rounds. Should they beat Comoros, the Super Falcons will move on to the third round in early 2027 to face either Morocco or the Democratic Republic of Congo. Subsequent rounds are set for late 2027, where potential clashes against sides like Cameroon, South Africa, or Zambia loom in the final stretch. The post Eguavoen appointed interim Super Falcons coach ahead of 2028 Olympic qualifiers appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Drought threatens Sudan’s agricultural season as food fears grow
items.description: Farmers and residents across parts of South Kordofan and Darfur are warning that severe rainfall shortages and prolonged dry spells are threatening this year’s agricultural season, raising fears of further food shortages and price rises. Residents in several areas of the Nuba Mountains told Radio Dabanga that rains have been scarce and interrupted, with unusually high temperatures damaging crops and threatening food security. In El Tadamon locality, residents said rainfall was below normal and insufficient for crops to continue growing, while the drought has extended across large areas. Residents of Abbasiya also warned that crops were increasingly vulnerable, raising fears of production losses, reduced food supplies and higher grain prices. A farmer in Abu Jubeiha told Radio Dabanga that drought had spread from the Habila and Liri agricultural projects through Abu Jubeiha, El Tadamon and Abbasiya, reaching areas south of Umm Rawaba. He said rains had stopped for more than 20 consecutive days amid severe and unusual heat . Some crops, particularly sorghum, sesame and peanuts, had been completely “burned” by the drought and could no longer be saved by later rainfall. Farmers have also reported unusually open roads between Abu Jubeiha and El Tadamon, and onwards to El Muqnas, Kosti, Talodi and Liri, allowing large trucks to move through areas where roads are normally disrupted during the autumn rains. The price of a sack of sorghum has risen from SDG70,000 to SDG120,000 amid the movement of crops from South Kordofan to El Obeid. No field surveys have yet been conducted in Abu Jubeiha by official, international or local organisations, making it difficult to estimate the scale of crop losses . Farmers said they had already lost money preparing land, buying inputs and paying labour, leaving them less able to prepare for the next season. Residents and farmers called for urgent field assessments, measures to restrict crop exports outside South Kordofan to protect local stocks, and immediate humanitarian intervention. ‘Darfur faces mounting drought’ Several areas of Darfur are also facing severe rainfall shortages, threatening agricultural production and raising concerns about food availability. In North Darfur, delayed and insufficient rains have left some farms dry while some farmers have yet to begin planting. Local emergency room members said villages west of Kutum and surrounding areas were facing a worsening crisis as delayed rains reduced pasture and water sources, threatening food security and livestock. It appealed for food, drinking water and support for water sources. In South Darfur, Adam El Fadil from Netika locality told Radio Dabanga that some farms had already reached the drought stage while others were waiting for rain before planting. He said cultivated millet had not yet reached half a metre, threatening basic crop production. He warned that food grain prices could rise to unaffordable levels. A sack of millet was selling for SDG280,000–300,000, while sorghum cost SDG220,000–230,000. Netika is among 13 South Darfur localities facing an emergency over rainfall shortages. In East Darfur, Hope and Refuge Organisations for Refugees and Support for Darfur Victims warned of rainfall shortages and agricultural failure in Abu Karinka. The group said rains had been interrupted for around three weeks, damaging large areas planted with millet and beans and forcing some farmers to use seed stocks, threatening next season’s planting. The organisation called on UN agencies, humanitarian organisations and donors to conduct an urgent assessment and provide food, seeds and agricultural inputs. ‘FAO warns of wider rainfall deficit’ The UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) reported that major agricultural areas in southeastern Sudan recorded significant rainfall deficits. Cumulative rainfall between June and mid-August was around 20 per cent below the long-term average in Sennar and 30 per cent below average in El Gedaref. FAO said severe moisture shortages had affected vegetation, with its Agricultural Stress Index showing severe drought across up to 40 per cent of cultivated land in Sennar and 70 per cent in El Gedaref. The agency warned that below-average rainfall during the June-September rainy season was already affecting germination and early crop development, while forecasts point to a high probability of below-average rainfall for the remainder of the planting season. Conflict has also disrupted farming in Darfur, Kordofan and Blue Nile, while insecurity , high input prices and limited access to credit continue to constrain agricultural production. FAO said sorghum prices rose by 65 per cent in most monitored markets between January and June, while millet prices increased by 42 per cent. Sudan’s 2025 cereal production stood at around 5.2 million tonnes, 22 per cent below 2024 levels and 19 per cent below the five-year average. The country is expected to need 2.8 million tonnes of cereal imports this year, mostly wheat, amid limited financial and logistical capacity. FAO estimates that 33.7 million people in Sudan will need assistance this year, including 19.5 million facing extreme hunger. items.title: Obi: HURIWA tackles Benue Govt over reported blockade
items.description: — Says those who stopped Obi couldn’t stop killings in Benue By Chioma Obinna LAGOS — The Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria, HURIWA, has condemned the reported blockade of the convoy of the presidential candidate of the National Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, while attempting to enter Benue State. HURIWA described the incident as “lawless, reckless and misdirected”, questioning the circumstances surrounding the reported confrontation and the decision to prevent Obi from proceeding into the state. In a statement by its National Coordinator, Comrade Emmanuel Nnadozie Onwubiko, the organisation said the incident was particularly troubling because Obi was reportedly visiting communities affected by attacks to commiserate with victims. The group said: “The mob that stopped Peter Obi failed to stop terrorists killing innocent Benue people.” HURIWA argued that attention should instead be focused on addressing insecurity affecting communities across the state. The organisation also questioned whether adequate security arrangements had been made to ensure the safety and free movement of Obi and his entourage. “We condemn the Benue State Government for permitting this lawlessness and we also blame the Federal Government for not deploying sufficient armed security forces to facilitate the passage of Peter Obi into Benue State,” HURIWA said. However, the organisation did not provide evidence linking the Benue State Government directly to the reported blockade. HURIWA recalled that Obi had previously encountered opposition while attempting to visit communities affected by insecurity in the state. It argued that citizens, including political leaders, should be able to visit communities affected by violence, subject to legitimate security considerations. “There is no known law allowing any government at the subnational or national level to prevent a Nigerian citizen from enjoying the constitutionally guaranteed rights to freedom of movement, association and information,” the group stated. HURIWA also questioned the basis for preventing Obi from entering the state, asking whether the governor had the authority to determine who could enter Benue. The rights group criticised what it described as the misplaced priority of confronting a politician visiting victims of attacks while insecurity remains a major concern in the state. It said it was a “shame” that a road blockade could occur over Obi’s visit while communities continued to face security challenges. HURIWA asked: “Is it not a shame that the Benue State Governor couldn’t mobilise youths and equip them with the requisite weapons to stop the incessant killings of Benue civilians by terrorists, but here are the youths being used for the political assignment of blocking the road so as not to allow Peter Obi to visit victims of terrorism in Benue State?” The group urged citizens not to allow political disagreements to escalate into confrontation, warning that such incidents could heighten political tension ahead of the next election cycle. According to reports cited by HURIWA, the incident occurred on Monday along Gboko Road as Obi and members of his entourage attempted to enter Benue State. A group reportedly blocked the convoy, leading to a confrontation before security personnel intervened. The circumstances surrounding the incident, including who organised the blockade, the precise reason for it and whether anyone was injured, were not independently established by HURIWA’s statement. HURIWA called on the National Security Adviser, Chief of Defence Staff, service chiefs and Inspector-General of Police to ensure that security agencies remained politically neutral and protected citizens’ rights. It also urged the police to investigate the incident and take appropriate action against anyone found to have committed an offence. HURIWA maintained that political disagreements should not be allowed to degenerate into violence or interfere with citizens’ fundamental rights. The organisation further criticised what it described as inadequate security arrangements for Obi, particularly amid reports that President Bola Tinubu had directed security agencies to strengthen protection for the opposition presidential candidate. HURIWA said the incident should serve as a warning that political tensions must not be allowed to undermine citizens’ rights or distract from the urgent need to tackle insecurity in Benue State. items.title: Tinubu mourns Peter Onwubuariri, media aide who served three presidents
items.description: President Bola Tinubu has mourned the death of Peter Onwubuariri, Assistant Director, Media, at the Presidential Villa and former North American Correspondent of the News Agency of Nigeria. Onwubuariri died after a prolonged illness, leaving behind a career spanning journalism, public service and media operations at the Presidential Villa. In a statement issued by his Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, in Abuja on Tuesday, Tinubu described the death as a painful loss to the Presidency, NAN, the media community and the country. Onwubuariri was posted from NAN to the Presidential Villa in 2014 and subsequently served under three successive administrations. He was part of the media teams of former Presidents Goodluck Jonathan and Muhammadu Buhari before continuing his service under Tinubu. The President described the deceased as a consummate journalist who covered several major national and international issues, including foreign affairs, telecommunications, politics and finance. Tinubu also commended his sound judgment and deep understanding of the relationship between government and the media. Before his posting to the Presidential Villa, Onwubuariri rose through the ranks at NAN and served as an Assistant Editor-in-Chief. The President said his contributions to journalism and NAN’s editorial operations reflected his dedication, professionalism and commitment to duty. “Peter was a dedicated journalist and a committed public servant whose professionalism and calm disposition earned him the respect of his colleagues and associates,” the President said. Tinubu said Onwubuariri’s service across three administrations demonstrated his competence, integrity and enduring commitment to national service. “His years of service to three administrations are a testament to his competence, integrity and commitment to duty,” he added. The President said the late journalist would be remembered for his diligence, wealth of experience and contributions to journalism and public service. “His passing is a great loss to the Presidential Villa, the media fraternity and Nigeria. He will be remembered for his diligence, his wealth of experience and his contributions to journalism and national service,” he added. Tinubu extended his condolences to Onwubuariri’s wife, Catherine, his three children, extended family, colleagues and friends. He prayed that God Almighty would grant the bereaved family the strength to bear the loss and grant the soul of the departed eternal rest. items.title: Ekiti Guber: Tribunal strikes out Oluyede’s petition against Oyebanji
items.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — The Ekiti State Governorship Election Petition Tribunal has struck out the petition filed by the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, governorship candidate, Dr Wole Oluyede, challenging the re-election of Governor Biodun Oyebanji of the All Progressives Congress, APC. The three-member tribunal, led by Justice Abubakar Idris Kutigi, struck out the petition at its first sitting in Ado-Ekiti on Tuesday following a motion for withdrawal filed by Oluyede. Other members of the panel are Justices Aminu Tukur and Maurice Okediya. The motion for withdrawal was moved by Oluyede’s counsel, Mr Paul Komolafe, who also represented the PDP. Counsel to Oyebanji and the APC, Dr Onyechi Ikpeazu, SAN, and counsel to the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, Sulaiman Ibrahim, did not oppose the application. Justice Kutigi subsequently struck out the petition in line with the petitioner’s request. INEC had declared Oyebanji winner of the June 20 governorship election after he polled 319,224 votes, while Oluyede garnered 40,543 votes. The African Democratic Congress, ADC, candidate, Chief Dare Bejide, came third with 12,872 votes. Speaking with journalists after the tribunal struck out his petition, Oluyede said he withdrew the case following appeals by individuals he considered important to him and out of respect for President Bola Tinubu. He said Oyebanji had also extended a hand of fellowship to him after the election and expressed readiness to work with him towards securing victory for Tinubu in Ekiti in the forthcoming presidential election. Oluyede said: “My decision (to withdraw the petition) was based on the fact that what Ekiti and Nigeria need now is to seek the way forward. “It’s not easy to withdraw your petition when you know you have a case, but I took the action at the request of people who are important to me, I mean the President and several advisers. “They have all asked me to withdraw the matter and advised that everybody should come together and let the President win the next election and bring Ekiti forward. “We have a lot of things to do in Ekiti and it will take the efforts of everybody. It shouldn’t be a partisan thing. “I am a member of PDP and still remain a member of PDP and we have an election in January for President Tinubu. The Governor too has extended a hand of friendship across to me and we will work together when the election comes and see how things go. It’s just for the betterment of Ekiti and Nigeria.” Meanwhile, the tribunal adjourned sitting to Thursday, September 10, for ruling on the pre-hearing report filed by parties and Monday, September 14, for hearing of the substantive petitions filed by the Social Democratic Party, SDP, and its candidate, Mr Isaac Adebayo Alade, as well as the Action Alliance, AA, and its candidate, Mr Matthew Olu Omotoso. The two parties and their candidates are challenging Oyebanji’s return as winner of the election by INEC. The SDP candidate polled 179 votes, while the AA candidate secured 126 votes in the election. The tribunal chairman advised counsel to the petitioners to ensure that the respondents were served in good time and that witnesses were brought to court on Monday for commencement of hearing. The tribunal subsequently fixed Thursday, September 10, for ruling on the pre-hearing report and Monday, September 14, for hearing of the substantive petitions. items.title: Burkina Faso : La BCLCC se dote d’un studio moderne pour traquer les fake news
items.description: Face à la prolifération des menaces numériques et de la désinformation, le Ministère de la Sécurité passe à l'offensive par la prévention. Le ministre de la Sécurité, le Camarade Mahamadou Sana, a officiellement inauguré, ce mardi après-midi 8 septembre 2026, le nouveau studio multimédia de la Brigade Centrale de Lutte contre la Cybercriminalité (BCLCC). Cette infrastructure moderne, équipée de technologies audiovisuelles de pointe, servira de centre névralgique pour la production de contenus éducatifs visant à déconstruire les fake news et à instaurer une véritable culture de la cybersécurité au sein de la population burkinabè. La lutte contre l'insécurité ne se joue plus seulement sur le terrain physique, mais également sur le terrain immatériel de l'information et des réseaux sociaux. Conscient de cet enjeu capital, le ministre de la Sécurité, le Camarade Mahamadou Sana, a présidé ce mardi après-midi 8 septembre 2026 l'inauguration du tout nouveau studio multimédia de la Brigade Centrale de Lutte contre la Cybercriminalité (BCLCC). Cet investissement d'envergure dotera l'institution d'une capacité de communication préventive moderne pour faire face à la sophistication croissante des menaces numériques. Doté d'équipements audiovisuels de dernière génération, ce nouveau pôle technologique aura pour mission principale la production de capsules vidéo et de contenus multimédias ciblés. Ces productions aborderont des thématiques cruciales, telles que la déconstruction systématique des fausses informations ( fake news ), la sensibilisation aux risques de piratage, et la vulgarisation de bonnes pratiques en matière d’utilisation des technologies de l'information et de la communication. Grâce à des formats pédagogiques adaptés et accessibles au grand public, la BCLCC souhaite toucher directement le citoyen afin de renforcer sa résilience et sa vigilance face aux pièges du cyberespace. Cette réalisation concrétise les orientations stratégiques du Gouvernement burkinabè, sous l'impulsion du Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. L'approche choisie démontre que la communication de proximité et la sensibilisation constituent désormais des leviers de sécurité nationale tout aussi indispensables que les mesures répressives. En donnant aux citoyens les clés pour identifier les contenus malveillants et sécuriser leurs données en ligne, la BCLCC s'érige en rempart contre la manipulation de l'opinion et accompagne de manière responsable la transition numérique du pays. items.title: AES: le médecin-colonel Romaric Toé prend les rênes du Réseau sahélien de médecine militaire
items.description: Le médecin-colonel Romaric Toé, directeur du service de santé des Armées, a pris, à Niamey, le lundi 7 septembre 2026, les rênes du Réseau sahélien de médecine militaire, lors d’un congrès, selon une information de Direction centrale du service de santé des armées. La Direction Centrale du Service de Santé des Armées (DCSSA) a pris part au 2ᵉ Congrès du Réseau sahélien de médecine militaire, tenu à Niamey, en marge des 2ᵉˢ Journées médico-chirurgicales. Réunissant les services de santé des Armées des trois pays de la Confédération des États du Sahel, ce congrès a constitué un cadre d’échanges, de partage d’expériences et de réflexion sur les enjeux, défis et perspectives de la médecine militaire dans l’espace sahélien. A cette rencontre, le médecin-colonel Romaric Toé « a été désigné Président du Conseil d’Administration (PCA) du Réseau sahélien de médecine militaire jusqu’en 2027 », lit-on dans un texte publié sur la page Facebook de la DCSSA. « Intervenant dans un contexte sécuritaire exigeant, qui appelle plus que jamais à une médecine militaire performante, résiliente et adaptée aux réalités opérationnelles, cette désignation traduit la confiance accordée au Burkina Faso et à son expertise dans le domaine de la santé militaire », souligne l’écrit qui ajoute que le médecin-colonel Toé. Le Médecin-Colonel Toé Romaric s’est engagé, au nom de l’équipe du Burkina Faso, à œuvrer pour l’atteinte des objectifs fixés par le Réseau. « Mon élection à ce Congrès constitue un appel à l’action et à la responsabilité », a-t-il déclaré. Par Wakat Séra L’article AES: le médecin-colonel Romaric Toé prend les rênes du Réseau sahélien de médecine militaire est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Cameroun: Kamto démissionne de la présidence du MRC
items.description: Coup de tonnerre dans l’opposition camerounaise. Maurice Kamto a annoncé, ce mardi 8 septembre 2026, sa démission de la présidence du Mouvement pour la renaissance du Cameroun (MRC). Une décision qu’il dit avoir prise dans «l’intérêt supérieur» du parti, de ses militants et du changement, sur fond de bras de fer avec le pouvoir de Paul Biya. Maurice Kamto n’est désormais plus le président du MRC. Le leader historique de la formation d’opposition a annoncé sa démission ce mardi 8 septembre 2026, dans une lettre publiée sur sa page Facebook. Après avoir dirigé le parti depuis sa création en 2012, l’opposant affirme vouloir préserver sa formation politique face aux pressions administratives. Cette démission intervient dans un contexte de «forte» tension avec le ministère camerounais de l’Administration territoriale. En décembre 2025, Maurice Kamto avait été réélu à la tête du MRC lors d’une convention extraordinaire. Mais le ministre Paul Atanga Nji a catégoriquement refusé de reconnaître cette réélection. Saisi par un dissident contestant le retour de Maurice Kamto à la direction du parti, le ministère de l’Administration territoriale avait, en août 2026, formellement décidé de ne pas prendre acte de son statut de président du MRC. En quittant la présidence, Maurice Kamto entend ainsi éviter que le bras de fer administratif ne se transforme en nouvelle crise interne. Le désormais simple membre du MRC dit agir pour protéger les intérêts de son parti et de ses militants, dans un contexte où les autorités sont accusées de chercher à fragiliser la formation politique. Mais la secousse ne s’est pas arrêtée à la démission du président. Dans la foulée, le premier vice-président du MRC, Mamadou Mota, a lui aussi annoncé son départ. Il dénonce «l’acharnement et l’oppression» continue du pouvoir contre leur formation politique. Cette démission intervient à un moment particulièrement sensible pour l’opposition camerounaise. Les élections législatives et municipales sont annoncées pour le début de l’année 2027, faisant peser une forte pression sur le MRC, qui devra rapidement réorganiser sa direction et être en mesure de faire valider ses listes de candidats. Le parti avait jusque-là boycotté les précédentes élections locales. Il se retrouve désormais face à un défi majeur, reconstruire son appareil dirigeant tout en préparant les prochaines échéances électorales, sans celui qui en était le visage depuis 2012. En quittant la tête du MRC, Maurice Kamto tourne une page importante de l’histoire de son parti, mais ouvre aussi une période d’incertitude. À quelques mois des élections de 2027, l’opposition camerounaise devra désormais démontrer qu’elle peut survivre à la disparition de son leader emblématique de la direction du parti. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Cameroun: Kamto démissionne de la présidence du MRC est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Bobo-Dioulasso : La Douane remet à l’armée des explosifs et du matériel saisis
items.description: Le ministère de l’Économie et des Finances, à travers la Direction générale des Douanes, a remis, ce 8 septembre 2026, au ministère de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique, un lot de produits saisis comprenant notamment des explosifs, des détonateurs et des cordons détonants. La cérémonie de remise s’est tenue à la Brigade mobile de Bobo-Dioulasso, à l’issue de la présentation, par le bureau des Douanes du port sec de Bobo-Dioulasso, de plus de 23 tonnes de riz impropres à la consommation. Les deux cérémonies se sont déroulées en présence du directeur général des Douanes, Dr Yves Kafando. Des mains du ministre de l’Économie et des Finances, Dr Aboubakar Nacanabo, le ministre d’État en charge de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique, le général de division Célestin Simporé, a réceptionné le lot de produits saisis par la Direction générale des Douanes. Celui-ci est composé de 2 013 bâtons d’explosifs, 47 rouleaux de cordons détonants, 3 284 détonateurs électriques, 107 équipements Starlink, 4 boîtiers de fibre optique, un rouleau de câble de connexion, 172 paires de chaussures de sécurité et 300 bidons de carburant de 25 litres. Le ministre d’État en charge de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique, le général de division Célestin Simporé, a salué la collaboration avec la douane -©️Faso7 Selon le ministre d’État en charge de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique, cette collaboration entre la Direction générale des Douanes et le département chargé de la Défense patriotique ne date pas d’aujourd’hui. Il a souligné que, sans cette saisie, ces produits auraient pu tomber entre les mains de groupes terroristes. « Cette collaboration entre la Douane et le ministère de la Défense ne date pas d’aujourd’hui. Depuis que nous sommes engagés dans cette guerre, nous bénéficions de l’appui de la Douane lorsqu’elle effectue des saisies de ce genre. Mais cette fois-ci, la prise est particulièrement importante » , a soutenu le général Célestin Simporé. Le ministre de l’Économie et des Finances, Dr Aboubakar Nacanabo, a annoncé l'intensification des actions de lutte contre la fraude par la douane -©️Faso7 Dans la même dynamique, le ministre de l’Économie et des Finances, Dr Aboubakar Nacanabo, a relevé que de nombreuses opérations douanières sont menées avec l’accompagnement des forces de défense et de sécurité. Il a saisi cette occasion pour appeler les acteurs impliqués dans des pratiques frauduleuses à y renoncer. « J’invite tous ceux qui sont dans les pratiques frauduleuses à faire attention, parce que la Douane va intensifier la lutte. Elle va continuer d’aller à l’offensive, parce qu’il faut assainir le marché et travailler à faire entrer les recettes » , a déclaré le Dr Aboubakar Nacanabo. Selon le ministre, la Douane entend ainsi intensifier la lutte contre la fraude afin d’assainir le marché et de renforcer la mobilisation des recettes publiques. 204 milliards de FCFA mobilisés au 31 août 2026 Présent à Bobo-Dioulasso dans le cadre d’un séjour de travail, le directeur général des Douanes, Dr Yves Kafando, s’est rendu, plus tôt dans la matinée, au bureau des Douanes du port sec de Bobo-Dioulasso, où il a pris part à la montée des couleurs nationales. Cette visite a également été l’occasion pour lui de féliciter ses collaborateurs pour les performances enregistrées. Le directeur général des Douanes s’est notamment réjoui des résultats de la région douanière de l’Ouest, qui regroupe les régions du Guiriko, des Tannounyan et du Bankuy. Du début de l’année au 31 août 2026, cette région a mobilisé 204 milliards de F CFA, pour une prévision de 191 milliards de F CFA sur la même période. Ces résultats représentent un excédent de 13 milliards de F CFA, soit un taux de recouvrement de 107 %. Dr Yves Kafando a exhorté les agents à maintenir cette dynamique, tout en les appelant à redoubler d’efforts face aux défis à venir. Il a rappelé que 104 milliards de F CFA restent encore à mobiliser au cours des quatre derniers mois de l’année, avant d’exprimer sa confiance dans la capacité de ses équipes à relever ce défi. Plus de 23 tonnes de riz impropres saisies D’une valeur de plus de 16 millions de FCFA, les sacs de riz impropres à la consommation humaine saisis auraient pu porter un coup dur à la santé des populations, a indiqué le directeur général des Douanes. Il a précisé que de la moisissure avait déjà proliféré sur une partie de la cargaison. Aperçu du riz prohibé Toutefois, l’ensemble de la cargaison n’a pas été saisi. Après des analyses en laboratoire, les sacs de riz jugés propres à la consommation ont été épargnés. « Ce sont plus de 20 tonnes de riz d'une valeur de plus de 16 millions de F CFA qui auraient pu porter un coup dur à la santé de nos population » , a déploré le Dr Yves Kafando. À noter que cette cargaison de riz était transportée par trois camions en provenance d’un pays voisin. Elle a transité par Niangoloko avant d’arriver à Bobo-Dioulasso. Faso7 L’article Bobo-Dioulasso : La Douane remet à l’armée des explosifs et du matériel saisis est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Gaïndé 2000 : « De la souveraineté numérique à l’accès numérique universel, financer l’avenir numérique de l’Afrique »
items.description: Ce 08 septembre 2026, durant cette première journée qui marque l’ouverture de la 5ème édition de la rentrée numérique Gaïndé 2000, le deuxième panel qui a porté sur le thème « De la souveraineté numérique à l’accès numérique universel : financer l’avenir numérique de l’Afrique » a donné la voix à différents acteurs du secteur numérique pour se prononcer sur les possibilités d’acquérir une connectivité numérique accessible à tous. Au cours des échanges, Mme Ndeye Fatou Ndiaye Blondin, coordonnatrice du FDSUT (Fonds de Développement du Service Universel des Télécommunications), est revenue sur la vocation première du FDSUT qui est « de connecter les zones rurales et de fournir aussi des services à des populations pas seulement rurales, mais plutôt à des institutions ». Mme Ndiaye Blondin informe par la même occasion qu’« ils ont fait un travail de vision stratégique de développement, un diagnostic de ce qu'est le service universel aujourd'hui ». En concluant, elle décline son espoir qu’« à travers le « New Deal », tout le secteur numérique pourra être financé » et que « le Code des télécommunications, qui a été rédigé il y a 10 ans et qui est en cours de révision, donnera aux fonds la mission de servir le service universel au sens large ». Panéliste de la session 2026 de la rentrée numérique, Papa Demba Thiam, économiste-architecte des transformations stratégiques, a annoncé le développement d’un instrument numérique appelé « PETIS 2.0 ». M. Thiam entend « concevoir avec son équipe » cet instrument « de telle manière à permettre à tous ceux qui veulent entreprendre d'accéder à la donnée qui est indispensable et dont ils ont besoin pour faire ça ». Le but de ce panel était « de décliner des solutions de financement innovantes et pérennes, au service à la fois de la souveraineté et de l’inclusion numérique du continent ». Fatou NGOM
